info.name: Dune Insolite - Tour/TourType/Extra Attributes + Reviews
info.description:
Covers every endpoint that is new or changed across this whole thread of work: POST/PUT on /api/tours, /api/tour-types, /api/extras (new fields: aboutText, highlights, includedItems, notIncludedItems, programSteps, meetingPoint, location, groupSizeType, languages, cancellationPolicy, coverPhotoUrl, photos, plus extraDuration on Extra only, plus isActive now exposed on TourType too); the /api/reviews subsystem; GetById/GetAll on all three now being public (no auth); the new PATCH .../deactivate soft-delete endpoints; and the ownership fix on GET /api/reservations/user/{userId}.

Run order matters for chaining (IDs/tokens are captured automatically via test scripts into collection variables): Auth -> Tours -> Tour Types -> Extras -> Reviews -> Deactivate -> Reservations -> Cleanup (deletes last, on purpose, so you can see review cascade-delete happen).

Before running: fill in adminEmail/adminPassword/clientAEmail/clientAPassword/clientBEmail/clientBPassword collection variables (or run the Register requests in the Auth folder first to create fresh test users), and make sure the backend is running on {{baseUrl}} against a live Postgres + Keycloak.

item.name: 0. Auth
Register Admin (optional, skip if you already have one)

request.description: Public endpoint. Creates the user directly in Keycloak + a local User row. `role` is required (no default) - must be exactly one of CLIENT, PARTENAIRE, CAMPING, ADMIN. Set adminEmail/adminPassword collection variables first.

item.name: Register Client A (optional)

request.description: Client A will be the one submitting reviews and testing the reservation ownership check. Set clientAEmail/clientAPassword collection variables first.

item.name: Register Client B (optional, needed for the 403 ownership tests)

request.description: Client B exists to prove Client B cannot edit Client A's review, and cannot read Client A's reservations (expect 403 both times). Skip this + those tests if you don't need that coverage.

item.name: Login as Admin

request.description: Public endpoint - proxies to Keycloak server-side, so you never need the Keycloak client secret. Captures accessToken + userId into collection variables automatically.

item.name: Login as Client A

request.description: Captures accessToken into {{clientAAccessToken}} and userId into {{clientAUserId}} (needed for the reservation-ownership tests).

item.name: Login as Client B

request.description: Captures accessToken into {{clientBAccessToken}} and userId into {{clientBUserId}}.

request.description: Requires ADMIN role (unchanged - only reads became public, not writes). On success, captures tourId into {{tourId}} for every later request in this collection.

exec: pm.test('location round-tripped', () => pm.expect(json.location).to.eql('Sabria, Douz, Sahara Tunisien'));
pm.test('highlights round-tripped', () => pm.expect(json.highlights).to.include('Nuit en bivouac sous les etoiles'));

pm.test('legacy duration field untouched', () => pm.expect(json.duration).to.eql('2 Jours / 1 Nuit'));
pm.test('averageRating starts null, reviewCount starts 0', () => { pm.expect(json.averageRating).to.be.null; pm.expect(json.reviewCount).to.eql(0); });

item.name: 4. Reviews (/api/reviews) - new subsystem
Create Review on Tour (Client A)

request.description: Any authenticated user. Author comes from the JWT (jwt.getSubject()), never from the request body. Saved immediately - no moderation/status step. Captures reviewIdOnTour.

item.name: Verify averageRating/reviewCount updated on the Tour

request.description: Re-fetches the Tour after the review above. This is the denormalized aggregate that gets recomputed on every review create/update/delete.

item.name: Create Duplicate Review on same Tour (Client A again) - expect 400

request.description: One review per (user, product) is enforced both in the service (friendly check) and at the DB level (unique constraint on user_id+product_id+product_type). Plain RuntimeException -> GlobalExceptionHandler maps it to 400 Bad Request with your message in the body.

item.name: Create Review with invalid rating (6) - expect 400 validation error

request.description: @Min(1)/@Max(5) on ReviewRequest.rating -> MethodArgumentNotValidException -> 400 with an `errors` field map (different body shape than the plain-RuntimeException 400 above - has a nested `errors.rating` message).

item.name: Create Review on nonexistent product - expect 400

request.description: Since Review.productId has no DB foreign key (mirrors the UserProductRemise/ProductType pattern already used elsewhere in this codebase), existence is checked in ReviewServiceImpl via existsById dispatched on productType before saving.

exec: pm.test('message mentions product not found', () => pm.expect(json.message).to.include('not found'));

item.name: Get Reviews for Tour (paginated)

request.description: Standard Spring Pageable query params (page/size/sort), @PageableDefault(size=10), same convention already used by /api/reservations. All reviews are visible immediately - there is no approved/pending filter.

item.name: Get Review by ID
Update Own Review (Client A changes rating to 4)

request.description: ReviewUpdateRequest only has rating+comment - reviewId/user/productId/productType/createdAt cannot be changed through this endpoint. Ownership is checked in the service (AccessDeniedException if not yours).

item.name: Verify averageRating updated on the Tour after edit
Update Someone Else's Review (Client B on Client A's review) - expect 403

request.description: Endpoint-level @PreAuthorize is just isAuthenticated() - ownership is enforced inside ReviewServiceImpl.updateReview via AccessDeniedException, which GlobalExceptionHandler already maps to 403 (no new handler was needed for this).

item.name: Delete Review (ADMIN)

request.description: Only ADMIN can delete a review directly (no moderation queue - this is the cleanup/abuse-removal path). Recomputes the parent Tour's aggregate afterward.

item.name: Verify averageRating cleared on the Tour after review deleted

exec: pm.test('averageRating is null again (no reviews left)', () => pm.expect(json.averageRating).to.be.null);

item.name: 5. Deactivate (soft delete)
Deactivate Tour (ADMIN)

request.description: Sets isActive=false and saves - does NOT delete the row. ADMIN only, same as the hard DELETE.

item.name: Verify Tour still exists (soft-deleted, not hard-deleted)

request.description: Proves this was a soft delete: the row is still fetchable by ID, just with isActive=false. It will also no longer appear in GET /api/tours/active.

exec: pm.test('Status is 200 - record still exists', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

item.name: Deactivate Tour Type (ADMIN)

request.description: Same pattern as Tour. This is also the first time TourType's isActive is reachable at all through the API, since it's now exposed on TourTypeResponse.

item.name: Verify Tour Type still exists (soft-deleted, not hard-deleted)

exec: pm.test('Status is 200 - record still exists', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

item.name: Deactivate Extra (ADMIN)
Verify Extra still exists (soft-deleted, not hard-deleted)

exec: pm.test('Status is 200 - record still exists', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

item.name: 6. Reservations - ownership check on /api/reservations/user/{userId}
Client A gets own reservations - expect 200

request.description: userId in the path equals the caller's own JWT subject, so this passes the new @PreAuthorize ownership check regardless of whether Client A has any reservations yet (an empty list is still 200 - this test is about authorization, not data).

exec: pm.test('Status is 200 - own reservations allowed', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

item.name: Client A gets Client B's reservations - expect 403

request.description: This is the exact gap that was fixed: before, any CLIENT/PARTENAIRE could pass an arbitrary userId and see someone else's full reservation history. Now the @PreAuthorize SpEL expression `hasAnyRole('ADMIN','CAMPING') or #userId.toString() == authentication.name` denies this.

exec: pm.test('Status is 403 Forbidden - cannot view another user\'s reservations', () => pm.response.to.have.status(403));

item.name: Admin gets Client A's reservations - expect 200

request.description: ADMIN bypasses the ownership check entirely - can fetch any userId's reservations.

exec: pm.test('Status is 200 - ADMIN can view any user', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

item.name: Admin gets Client B's reservations - expect 200

request.description: Same as above, different target userId - confirms the ADMIN bypass isn't accidentally hardcoded to one specific user.

exec: pm.test('Status is 200 - ADMIN can view any user', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

item.name: 7. Cleanup (run last - proves review cascade-delete)
Create one more Review on the Tour (to prove cascade on delete)

request.description: Client B (not Client A, who already has a deleted one) leaves a fresh review so there's something for the Delete Tour request below to cascade-delete. Works even though the Tour was deactivated earlier - deactivate only flips isActive, reviews are unaffected.

item.name: Delete Tour (ADMIN) - also deletes its remaining reviews

request.description: TourServiceImpl.deleteTour now also calls reviewRepository.deleteAllByProductIdAndProductType(tourId, TOUR) right alongside the pre-existing userProductRemiseRepository cleanup call. This is the hard delete - separate from the deactivate (soft delete) tested above.

item.name: Verify the Tour's reviews are gone (list returns empty)

request.description: The Tour itself is gone (previous request), but this call still succeeds since GET /api/reviews doesn't validate product existence - it should just come back with an empty page, proving the cascade delete worked.

exec: pm.test('no reviews left for the deleted tour', () => pm.expect(json.content).to.have.lengthOf(0));
